newsitem.title: USA: Farm Family sees Q4 retirement plan charge.
newsitem.headline: Farm Family sees Q4 retirement plan charge.

text.p: Farm Family Holdings Inc said on Monday it expected to take about an $0.11 per share or $600,000 charge in the fourth quarter because it was implementing a voluntary early retirement program.
The company said it would also make other changes to the company's benefit plans, as part of its ongoing expense management program.
The retirement plan would be offered "to over 60 employees" and is set to be completed in April 1997, the company said.
The company said the anticipated fourth quarter charge would be non-recurring and offset by savings from the plan.
The company said it estimated the early retirement plan would result in savings, net of tax, of about $150,000 to $225,000 per year, or between $0.03 and $0.04 per share.

The board also approved changes to the Farm Family's employee benefit plans. The company said it would freeze benefits available through its defined benefit plan and enhance its defined contribution plan.
The result of this action was that employee retirement contributions would vary more than before based on Farm Family's profitability, the company said.
The board also approved a stock option plan and an annual incentive plan for company officers, the company said.
